01 · Analytical design

Time is part of the problem.

A random split would blend different risk regimes and overstate probability stability. Every stage receives its own chronological window, and the final 14 weeks stay locked until evaluation.

Chronological evidence chain

No cohort is reused for tuning, calibration, policy selection or final reporting.

DevelopmentW0–541,129,770 cases3.13% default
CalibrationW55–68171,375 cases4.51% default
PolicyW69–7773,807 cases2.35% default
Locked OOTW78–91151,707 cases2.12% default
Prevalence or maturity shift

OOT target prevalence is 32.2% below development and weekly volume is 47.2% lower. The public target exposes no label-window end date, so population drift and right-censoring cannot be separated.

Leakage boundary

Identifiers, file partitions, decision month and cohort fields never enter the model. Absolute dates become days before the decision.

02 · Model evidence

Strong ranking. Honest calibration.

The challenger materially improves future-cohort discrimination. The dashboard also exposes its weakness: a score calibrated in a high-default window overpredicts risk when prevalence falls.

03 · Decision lab

Move the approval frontier.

Choose a policy target and LGD scenario. Cut-offs were selected on policy weeks and applied unchanged to locked OOT—so the result measures transfer, not retrospective optimisation.

04 · Explainability

Evidence, not decoration.

Candidate reason codes come from the largest positive local log-odds contribution in a deterministic 10,000-case OOT sample. Only aggregate prevalence is published.

Explanation boundary

These are internal diagnostic candidates—not customer-facing adverse-action notices.

  • Global importance is not a reason code.
  • Correlation does not establish causality.
  • Direction and semantics need validation.
  • Legal suitability requires jurisdiction review.
05 · Model risk

What would make us stop?

A deployable lending model needs explicit monitoring and reversal conditions. Good OOT discrimination is necessary, but it is not permission to automate adverse action.

Investigate at 0.10; treat 0.25 as a population-drift breach.

Warning and breach thresholds relative to the validated reference.

2.0 / 5.0 pp

Calibration gap

Monitor only after outcomes mature; refresh an intercept before refitting rank.

Recommended next decision

Run the challenger in shadow mode, retain decision-time inputs, validate reason-code consistency, complete protected-group testing with lawful audit attributes, and compare model recommendations with reviewer overrides.
